title: What If TSF: Evaluating Scenario-Guided Multimodal Time Series Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2601.08509v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled time series forecasting to move beyond numerical observations and incorporate external information in multimodal settings. Such information can improve forecasting performance, but accuracy alone may not reveal whether models appropriately respond to it: a model may ignore relevant information, fail to distinguish scenarios with different implications, or overreact to irrelevant or weak signals. We introduce What If TSF (WIT), a benchmark for evaluating whether models effectively respond to future scenarios. WIT constructs controlled scenario sets by fixing the forecasting state while systematically varying future scenarios, enabling three complementary evaluations: Factual Comparison, which measures the predictive utility of factual scenario information; Relational Comparison, which evaluates whether forecasts satisfy expected direction, contrast, intensity, and restraint

translated_title: What If TSF：评估场景引导的多模态时间序列预测
translated_abstract: 近期大语言模型的进展使时间序列预测得以超越纯数值观测，在多模态设置中融入外部信息。这类信息可以提升预测性能，但仅凭准确率可能无法揭示模型是否恰当地响应了这些信息：模型可能忽略相关信息、无法区分具有不同含义的场景，或对无关或微弱信号过度反应。我们提出了 What If TSF（WIT），一个用于评估模型是否有效响应未来场景的基准。WIT 通过固定预测状态的同时系统地变化未来场景，构建受控场景集，从而支持三种互补的评估：事实比较，衡量事实场景信息的预测效用；关系比较，评估预测是否满足预期的方向、对比、强度与克制等关系。
tldr: 该论文提出了WIT基准，通过固定预测状态并系统变化未来场景构建受控场景集，以评估多模态时间序列预测模型能否恰当响应未来场景信息。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces WIT, a benchmark that evaluates whether multimodal time series forecasting models effectively respond to future scenarios by constructing controlled scenario sets that fix the forecasting state while systematically varying future scenarios.
